summary: Florin Deleanu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bucharest, Peking, Waseda, and Hamburg under Bunga Fukui, Takashi Iwata, and Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at Kansai Medical University, Hamburg, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Florinda De Simini works in Indology. She studied at the University of Turin under Francesco Sferra, Harunaga Isaacson, and Peter C. Bisschop. Her career includes posts at IIAS, University of Naples Federico II, and University of Naples "L'Orientale".

Fokke Sierksma was a religious studies and Tibetology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Groningen in 1950. He worked at the Groningen University Library before serving as Lecturer and later Professor of History of Religion at Leiden University.

Folke Bergman worked in archaeology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala University and served as Amanuens of East Asian collections at the Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities from around 1935 to 1946.

Forbes Falconer studied Classics at Aberdeen and Marischal College, later studying under Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, and Heinrich Ewald. Working in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he became Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindustani at UCL in 1834.

Forster Fitzgerald Arbuthnot, active in Indology, studied at East India Company College in 1851. He served in the Indian Civil Service from 1853 to 1878 as Collector of Bombay City and Island, and founded the Kama Shastra Society.

Frances Garrett is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who held a post at the University of Virginia (attested 1997). She serves as Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto (attested 2026).
Frances W. Pritchett is an Indology scholar who held a post at Columbia University from around 1982 to 2013, becoming Professor Emeritus around 2013.

Frances Wood studied at Newnham College, Cambridge, and Peking University, specializing in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Central Asian studies. She served at the British Library from around 1977 to 2013 and worked as a Clinical Psychologist at North Bristol NHS Trust in 2023.
Francesca Fremantle is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London from 1968 to 1971 and under Chögyam Trungpa between 1971 and 1975.

Francesca Tarocco earned her PhD at SOAS University of London in 2005. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, she became Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 2016 and Visiting Associate Professor at NYU Shanghai in 2017.

Francesco Adolfo Cannizzaro, working in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied under Angelo De Gubernatis from around 1891 to 1893 and completed a degree in law at the University of Catania in 1894.

Francesco Cimmino studied Indology at Naples under Michele Kerbaker and at Turin under Giovanni Flechia. He taught at Liceo Antonio Genovesi before serving as docent and then Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Naples Federico II from 1914 to 1935.

Francesco Lorenzo Pullè studied under De Gubernatis, Weber, Mommsen, and Kiepert. An Indology and linguistics scholar, he held professorships at the University of Padua (1875–1889) and the University of Bologna (1899–1925), and also held a post at Pisa.

Francesco Ribezzo studied under Michele Kerbaker at Naples, at Leipzig, and under Alfredo Trombetti. A scholar of linguistics and archaeology, he taught at Naples, became docent at Messina, and served as Professor at the University of Palermo from 1925 to 1948.

Francesco Scerbo studied under Angelo De Gubernatis and Antelmo Severini. Focusing on linguistics and Indology, he taught Hebrew at the University of Florence as libero docente from 1892 and incaricato from 1903 to 1924.

Francesco Sferra, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studied under Raniero Gnoli and Raffaele Torella. He has held positions at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Naples Federico II.

Francis A. Wood, a linguist, earned degrees from Northwestern and the University of Chicago and studied at Göttingen. He served as Professor at Chaddock College and Cornell College before becoming Assistant Professor at the University of Chicago from 1903 to 1927.

Francis Balfour was active in Indology and received his Dr.Med. from the University of Edinburgh by 1767. He served in the East India Company as Assistant Surgeon starting in 1769 and as full surgeon from 1777 to 1807.

Francis Brandt earned his B.A. from the University of Oxford and Brasenose College. Active in Indology and linguistics, he served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1862 to 1889 and as Lecturer in Tamil and Indian Law at Cambridge from 1891 to 1895.
